architecture.mechanism: Localized corrosion is initiated by crevice corrosion at aluminum inclusions and accelerated by galvanic coupling where cementite in pearlite acts as a cathode to promote dissolution of surrounding ferrite.
architecture.intervention: Inject a targeted cathodic inhibitor slurry into the annular space at sleeve joints through small access ports to suppress the cathodic reduction reaction on cementite phases, halting the galvanic acceleration of pitting without excavation or relining.
architecture.expected_effect: Suppression of the cathodic half-reaction eliminates the galvanic driving force for ferrite dissolution, arresting the propagation rate of existing chloride-induced pits and extending pipe service life beyond the 25-year premature failure point.
architecture.falsification_test: Extract coupon samples from treated sleeve joint annular spaces after 6 months and measure pit depth progression via optical profilometry; if pit depth growth rate matches untreated control sections, the intervention failed.
